observations.why: The gate is framed as a security requirement before deployment, appealing to conservation of safety.
Citing past failures as justification for the gate appeals to security and quality-of-craft concerns.
Restates the gate as a security mandate; conservation of safety is the appealed-to good.
Extending the security gate across environments appeals to conservation of stability.
Claiming ownership of the gate positions the speaker as the authority behind it, appealing to standing.
